patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.quote: I fell on my arm playing football and my shoulder popped out of place — I can feel it's not sitting right. I'm holding it away from my body because I can't move it at all.
presentation.triageNote: 22-year-old male who fell onto his arm playing football. The shoulder has a squared-off contour and he holds the arm slightly away from his body and externally rotated; movement is severely limited, with intact distal circulation and sensation.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player's assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 3 is appropriate because a stable shoulder dislocation is expected to require multiple resources including imaging, analgesia or sedation, and reduction.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This patient has an obvious shoulder deformity after trauma with preserved distal neurovascular status.
clinical.acuityReason: The injury is not currently limb-threatening, but severe motion restriction and deformity require imaging and a monitored reduction procedure.
expectedResources: Analgesia and procedural sedation as needed
keyFindings: Arm held abducted and externally rotated
teachingPoints: Axillary-nerve and distal neurovascular findings should be recorded before and after reduction.
Post-reduction imaging and immobilization help confirm alignment and identify associated fracture.

possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: Imaging and monitored reduction would likely be followed by immobilization, repeat examination, and orthopedic follow-up.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.pose: seated with injured right arm held away from the torso, elbow bent, forearm externally rotated, and uninjured hand resting on thigh
aiImageGeneration.expression: alert, pained, and tense while looking toward the injured shoulder
signs: clear gap between injured elbow and torso with the forearm held forward and palm up
flattened, squared-off lateral shoulder contour with a subtle hollow below the acromion
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Create a new square isolated patient character asset matching the attached anchor's softly shaded painterly semi-realistic clinical illustration style, same white 22-year-old athletic man, red football jersey, black shorts, sneakers, and blue padded clinic chair. BACKGROUND: perfectly uniform solid pure chroma green #00FF00 edge to edge, with no floor, shadow, gradient, texture, scenery, vignette, or green spill. This will be removed to transparency. CRITICAL POSE—follow literally: the patient's INJURED RIGHT ARM appears on the VIEWER'S LEFT side of the picture. His injured right upper arm hangs slightly abducted, leaving a clear visible gap between elbow and torso. The injured right shoulder has a flattened, squared-off outer contour and a subtle hollow beneath the acromion instead of a normal rounded deltoid. His injured elbow is bent about 90 degrees, and the right forearm points forward and slightly upward with palm facing up, demonstrating external rotation. The injured arm must remain entirely on the viewer's left side and must NOT cross the chest, abdomen, lap, or body midline. His uninjured left hand rests open on his left thigh and does not touch or hold the injured arm. He looks down toward the abnormal shoulder with a tense, pained expression. Show full body and entire chair with margins; exactly one person, two anatomically plausible arms and hands, two legs and feet. No elbow deformity, no wrist injury, no forearm fracture, no crossed arms, no hand clutching an upper arm, no sling, blood, bruising, medical equipment, text, labels, logos, or jersey numbers.
